cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: Both papers (single source) confirm that while quantitative results (290 nm size, 69 vol% volume fraction, spherical morphology) and qualitative images (Fig. 1b carbide morphology) are presented for the High Entropy Superalloy, the specific experimental parameters defining these measurements are omitted.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The inquiry is split into two distinct methodological gaps within the same source: one addressing the imaging hardware settings (SEM voltage/magnification) required to resolve the carbide morphology, and the other addressing the computational geometry definitions used to derive the 290 nm precipitate size.

cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No contradictions exist between the answers; they independently report the absence of specific data points in the source text.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Strong negative evidence: The source explicitly acknowledges the presence of the data (290 nm, Fig. 1b) but admits the absence of the defining parameters.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The exact geometric definition of the 'average size' for the γ′ precipitates and the specific SEM operating conditions used to capture the carbide morphology remain unidentified.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The study likely utilized standard image analysis protocols where 'average size' refers to equivalent circular diameter, and SEM imaging was performed at a standard voltage (e.g., 15-20 kV) and magnification sufficient for 300 nm features, though these were not explicitly documented in the text.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Re-imaging the same sample under varying SEM magnifications and voltages while manually applying both Feret and equivalent diameter calculations would determine if the reported 290 nm value aligns with a specific metric and if the carbide morphology resolution is voltage-dependent.
